title: Creating and opening files; file modes and fopen
learningObjectives: Explain the C concept and its rules.
Trace the example and describe data flow.
Identify relevant failure and boundary cases.
Apply the concept in a tested C program.

understand.concept: fopen opens a file stream using a path and mode string. Modes such as r, w and a select reading, truncating/creating for writing, or appending; adding b requests binary mode where relevant. fopen returns a FILE pointer or NULL on failure.
understand.whyItMatters: File operations interact with the environment and can fail because of missing paths, permissions, resource limits or storage errors. Every open must be checked and every successfully opened stream must be closed.
understand.analogy: Treat the operation as a clearly specified contract between the program and its data.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace C's type, lifetime, I/O and object representation rules.

explain.narrative:
fopen opens a file stream using a path and mode string. Modes such as r, w and a select reading, truncating/creating for writing, or appending; adding b requests binary mode where relevant. fopen returns a FILE pointer or NULL on failure.

Check all return values, object lifetimes, types and preconditions. Enable compiler warnings and test expected as well as failure paths.

examples.title: Focused C example
examples.explanation: The w mode creates the file or truncates an existing file. The program checks fopen before using the stream and checks fclose for a possible write/close error.

practise.guidedTask: Compare r, w, a, r+, w+ and a+ modes.
practise.independentTask: Write a program that opens a file in append mode, reports errors and closes the stream on every successful-open path.
hints: Use a path appropriate to the program's working directory and platform.
Do not assume a relative path is relative to the source file; it is normally relative to the process working directory.
Check fclose because buffered output errors may be reported when closing.
